analytes.label: Limonene
analytes.stereoNote: Chiral. Routine cannabis testing on achiral GC columns reports total limonene without resolving (R)-(+) and (S)-(−) enantiomers. Biosynthesis work characterised a cannabis (−)-limonene synthase (Günnewich et al. 2007; Booth et al. 2017), while some aroma literature refers to D-(+)-limonene (Oswald et al. 2023). The enantiomeric composition of a given sample is therefore unknown.

analytes.label: β-Caryophyllene
analytes.stereoNote: PubChem CID 5281515 is (−)-trans-caryophyllene, the naturally predominant form. Labs report 'caryophyllene' or 'β-caryophyllene'; caryophyllene oxide is a separate oxidation product and is not included here.

analytes.label: α-Pinene
analytes.stereoNote: Chiral. Labs report total α-pinene. A cannabis (+)-α-pinene synthase has been characterised (Günnewich et al. 2007; Booth et al. 2017), but sample enantiomer ratios are not reported.

analytes.label: β-Pinene
analytes.stereoNote: Chiral; labs report total β-pinene with stereochemistry unresolved.

analytes.label: Linalool
analytes.stereoNote: Chiral. (R)-(−)-linalool (licareol) and (S)-(+)-linalool (coriandrol) are distinct compounds; routine testing reports their total.

analytes.label: α-Humulene
analytes.stereoNote: Achiral ring with defined (E) double-bond geometry; formerly called α-caryophyllene, a ring-opened isomer of β-caryophyllene.

analytes.label: Ocimene (isomer total)
analytes.stereoNote: Labs report one or more geometric isomers — (E)-β-ocimene, (Z)-β-ocimene and sometimes α-ocimene — that are separate compounds. The Smith et al. dataset sums all reported ocimene isomers into one total; this analyte is that total, not a single compound.

analytes.label: Nerolidol (isomer total)
analytes.stereoNote: (E)-(trans) and (Z)-(cis)-nerolidol are distinct geometric isomers, each also chiral at C3. Smith et al. sum cis, trans and unspecified nerolidol into one total; the CT registry reports cis and trans separately.

analytes.label: α-Bisabolol
analytes.stereoNote: Has two stereocentres. (−)-α-Bisabolol (levomenol, CID 442343) is the well-known natural form, but cannabis lab reports do not specify the stereoisomer, so the stereo-unspecified record is the reference.

analytes.label: Borneol
analytes.stereoNote: PubChem CID 64685 leaves the stereocentres undefined. Borneol (endo) and isoborneol (exo, CID 6321405) are diastereomers; the CT registry reports them as separate analytes and only 'borneol' is mapped here.

analytes.label: Fenchol
analytes.stereoNote: Also called fenchyl alcohol. CID 15406 leaves stereocentres undefined; labs do not specify the isomer. Not to be confused with fenchone, a ketone reported separately.

analytes.label: Geraniol
analytes.stereoNote: The (E) isomer; its (Z) isomer nerol is a separate compound reported separately.

analytes.label: γ-Terpinene
analytes.stereoNote: Achiral. A positional isomer of α-terpinene and terpinolene.

contextCompounds.label: 3-Methyl-2-butene-1-thiol
contextCompounds.note: Not a terpene. Identified by Oswald et al. (2021) as the primary odorant behind the characteristic 'skunk-like' aroma of cannabis, present at trace levels that routine terpene panels do not measure.

contextCompounds.label: Skatole (3-methylindole)
contextCompounds.note: Not a terpene. Oswald et al. (2023) identified skatole as the key source of the 'chemical' aroma in some cultivars and argued that the importance of terpenes to cannabis aroma has been overemphasised.
